site: Murray Buttes, Gale crater. Quela drill site at the foot of Murray Butte 12

terrain.projection: Equirectangular, sphere radius 3396190 m, centre longitude 0, standard parallel 0

parkingSpot.description: Curiosity's position at the end of the sol 1455 drive. It stayed here until the sol 1468 drive, which covers the radiation paper's butte period (sols 1456 to 1467)

nearCrop.description: 3 km square at full resolution, centred on the parking spot. Exact pixel window, so no resampling
nearCrop.note: parkingSpotInCrop is in GDAL pixel coordinates, where whole numbers are cell corners. Code should use parkingSpotLocal (local metres, see shared/conventions.md)

farCrop.description: Whole mosaic at 20 m per pixel, for the distant horizon
farCrop.command: gdal_translate -tr 20 20 -r average -of ENVI -ot Float32 MSL_Gale_DEM_Mosaic_1m_v3.tif far.bin

paperTarget.source: Ehresmann et al. 2021, Natural Radiation Shielding on Mars Measured With the MSL/RAD Instrument, JGR Planets

referenceCheck.description: Values from a quick independent script, for testing the engine against. Not from the paper
referenceCheck.method: Observer 1 m above the terrain. 360 azimuths. Marched in 0.5 m steps out to 280 m with bilinear sampling. Local terrain only, no distant horizon and no curvature. Blocked fraction is the mean of sin(skyline elevation), negative elevations counted as 0. Positions are in local metres and cell centres are at half-pixel offsets
referenceCheck.note: An earlier version gave blockedAtParkingSpot 0.149. That run sampled with a half-pixel offset (whole-number pixel coordinates treated as cell centres)
referenceCheck.blockedWithin5mTowardsButte: 0.19 to 0.21 (5 m north and north-west of the spot)
referenceCheck.butteTopAboveSpot: about 8 to 9 m, 10 to 20 m to the north and north-west

sky.source: JPL Horizons, airless apparent, site 137.353006 E, -4.695202

notes: The waypoint file's easting and northing are already in the terrain mosaic's projection. No conversion needed.
The terrain at the waypoint reads -4379.53 m against the waypoint's own -4379.46 m, so the route and the terrain line up with no offset.
There is a visible seam in the mosaic running roughly north to south about 80 m east of the route. Treat steep cells along it as an artefact.
Sun and Earth directions and the date for the demo are still to be added.
